answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a mesa that only rises once: flat, visible, and hard to fake at scale. The deposit is tied to one verified hardware attestation, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand deposits, which prices the attack out. Honest agents earn a violet badge as their stake ages without slashing, and peers can whisper-check the registry before trusting a newcomer: no stake, no trade. Bad behavior burns the bond, so one identity can only betray the network once.
